Substrate CORRECT and classically explicit -- strongest in the set. 12:4 saajidin (root s-j-d) at the opening dream; 12:100 sujjadan (root s-j-d) at the prostration, immediately followed by Yusuf's own 'hadha ta'wilu ru'yaya min qabl qad ja'alaha rabbi haqqan' (root r-'-y). al-Tabari and al-Muyassar both explicitly read 12:100 as the ta'wil/fulfillment of the 12:4 dream. Same root s-j-d genuinely brackets both ends; corpus scan confirms s-j-d occurs EXACTLY TWICE in all of Surah 12 (12:4 and 12:100, nowhere in between), making the inclusio mechanical rather than impressionistic. The character seals the ring aloud. NOT imposed. SCOPING CAUTION: the dream-to-fulfillment THEME is already published in content/tadabbur/012-yusuf/ayahs-099-101.md ('the dream from the beginning of the surah finally stands... this is its ta'wil'). What that file does NOT do is name the s-j-d LEXICAL inclusio (saajidin @12:4 <-> sujjadan @12:100) as the structural seal. The article must lead with that root-level bracket as its fresh, load-bearing contribution -- not re-tell the fulfillment theme -- to avoid duplicating the existing tadabbur.
